inspiration.observed_pattern: A cross-database SQL macro exposes REGEXP_INSTR with explicit starting-position and occurrence arguments so callers can locate a selected regular-expression match rather than only test whether text matches.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent incident-message offset audit using MariaDB 10.11.7's compatible two-argument REGEXP_INSTR form. Fixed message text exercises first-match, nonmatching, and NULL behavior; the source macro's adapter dispatch, schema, and values are not copied.

fixture_notes: Message 901 contains two incident tokens, message 902 has none, message 903 is NULL, and message 904 begins with one token before a later second token. The first matching offset, zero no-match result, and NULL propagation must be observable.
determinism_notes: Message IDs and text are fixed; output is ordered by the unique message ID with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE incident_messages (message_id INT PRIMARY KEY, message_text VARCHAR(128) NULL)
INSERT INTO incident_messages VALUES (901, 'Queue ERR-17 then ERR-23'), (902, 'No incident marker'), (903, NULL), (904, 'ERR-31 at start and ERR-44 later')

steps.sql: SELECT message_id, REGEXP_INSTR(message_text, 'ERR-[0-9]+') AS first_offset FROM incident_messages ORDER BY message_id
